children: Bank Nifty outperformed benchmark indices on September 18 and rose above 56,400 with HDFC Bank leading the gains.
The heavyweight bank stock rose over 2.5%, followed by Punjab National Bank and IndusInd Bank, which rose 0.6% each. Other gainers in the sectoral index are Axis Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank.
At 2:15 pm on September 18, Bank Nifty was trading 0.65% higher at 56,426.55, thus outperforming benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty, whichclimbed 0.4%.

"The broader structure remains cautious, with the index continuing to trade below key resistance levels and yet to establish a sustained Higher High–Higher Low formation. 55,700–55,800 remains the immediate support zone, marked by the identical lows of the last two sessions. Holding above this zone is crucial to maintain the current consolidation; a break below 55,700 would resume the broader corrective trend and open downside towards 55,200 and 54,800 levels.

"On the higher side, Thursday’s high of 56,570 will acts as an immediate hurdle. A sustained move above this level could trigger a recovery towards the key resistance of 57,000 levels," said Pabitro Mukherjee, Deputy Vice President-Research, Bajaj Broking.

"On the downside, immediate support is placed at 55,800, while resistance is seen at 56,500. Positional support remains at 55,500. A decisive break below 55,800 could intensify selling pressure in the index," said Vatsal Bhuva, Technical Analyst at LKP.

"The immediate resistance is positioned near 56,600, and a decisive move above this level could lead to an up move towards 57,000. On the downside, support is placed around 55,700. A break below this level could trigger further weakness, potentially taking the index towards 55,500," said Axis Securities.

title: Bank Nifty outperforms benchmarks, rises above 56,400; HDFC Bank jumps over 2.5%: What lies ahead?
